message.content: Trade shaped the pharaoh’s powers. It gave them gold, grain, wood, and luxury goods. They used it to fund temples, armies, and projects. It strengthened his authority, made his court richer, and raised their prestige. We can see that it also tied their fate to routes; if they lost them, their power declined. You should note that it gave their rivals new leverage, and their enemies could exploit it. Our point is that it made the pharaoh both stronger and more vulnerable, because it connected their wealth to distant lands.
